title: `--network=host` breaks CDI device resolution on container start
body:
### Issue Description

A container requesting a CDI device (`nvidia.com/gpu=all` or a concrete device name like `nvidia.com/gpu=0`) fails to start with:

``` 
Error: unable to start container "...": setting up CDI devices: unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all
```

**if and only if `--network=host` is also used.** The same CDI device resolves and starts successfully with any other network mode (including the default bridge), and `--privileged` on its own has no effect on this.



### Steps to reproduce the issue


```
podman create --name t1 --privileged --device nvidia.com/gpu=all alpine sleep 5
podman start t1
# -> succeeds resolving CDI (fails later, unrelated: default bridge networking
#    hits a separate missing-iptables-xt_comment-module issue in this environment)

podman create --name t2 --network=host --device nvidia.com/gpu=all alpine sleep 5
podman start t2
# -> Error: unable to start container "...": setting up CDI devices:
#    unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all
```

Also reproduces with a concrete (non-aggregate) device name instead of `all`:

```
podman create --name t3 --network=host --device nvidia.com/gpu=0 alpine sleep 5
podman start t3
# -> Error: unable to start container "...": setting up CDI devices:
#    unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=0
```                                                                                                                          

Reproduces identically whether the container is created via:
- the CLI, as two separate `create`/`start` invocations
- the CLI, as a single `podman run` — **note:** `podman run` without `--network=host`/`--privileged` succeeds at CDI resolution, so this specific combination wasn't tested standalone via `podman run`; the isolation above (`--network=host` alone vs `--privileged` alone) was done via separate `create`+`start`
- the REST API (via `podman-py`'s `containers.run()`, which internally does a `POST /containers/create` followed by a separate `POST /containers/{id}/start`)

The `journalctl -u podman.service` log confirms `containers/create` returns `201` successfully in all cases; the CDI error is raised specifically during the later `POST /containers/{id}/start` call.




### Describe the results you received

As per description:
```
Error: unable to start container "...": setting up CDI devices: unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all 
```


### Describe the results you expected

CDI device resolution during container start should not depend on the container's network mode. `--network=host` should not prevent `nvidia.com/gpu=*` CDI devices from resolving.

- Podman itself is running inside a Docker container (nested containerization)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060, driver present, `nvidia-smi -L` works fine on the host
- NVIDIA Container Toolkit CDI spec present and valid at `/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml` and `/var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml` (mode 644, root:root), regenerated fresh with `nvidia-ctk cdi generate` immediately before testing
- `nvidia-ctk cdi list` correctly resolves 3 devices: `nvidia.com/gpu=0`, `nvidia.com/gpu=GPU-6a355609-acfb-7336-55f8-da85ddace403`, `nvidia.com/gpu=all`

Yes

### Privileged Or Rootless
